summary: Well-executed preregistered paired experiment testing a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline for LLM-produced vendor-CLI configs. Strong reproducibility artifacts and mandatory provenance present. The primary inferential pipeline was followed, but a preregistered sensitivity analysis that was promised in the preregistration was omitted from the reported confirmatory results. References are listed as DOIs in the manuscript evidence bundle and the manuscript must present a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with each cited record verified to support the proximate claim. Given these resolvable defects, the manuscript is scientifically valuable but requires targeted revisions before finalisation.
critical_issues: A preregistered sensitivity analysis (treating failed episodes/pairs as failures per the preregistration: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') was not executed or reported as part of the confirmatory results despite being promised in the preregistration. This omission affects interpretation of the primary finding and must be resolved by adding the pre-registered sensitivity analysis results (or, if it truly was not executed, explicitly stating in Methods and Results that it was not executed and limiting claims accordingly).

The References/ citation presentation must be converted to a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (full bibliographic metadata: authors, title, venue, year) rather than numbered bare DOI entries or DOI-only identifiers, and each cited reference must be verified to actually support the nearby scholarly claim. The current cited_record_ids list DOIs only; the manuscript must supply standard IEEE reference entries (resolvable from supplied artifacts) and ensure citation semantics are correct.
required_revisions: Execute and report the preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats failed episodes/pairs as failures (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity), using the archived execution artifacts only; include numeric results, confidence bounds, and interpretive impact on the primary inference in Methods/Results and update Conclusions accordingly. If the analysis truly was not run, explicitly state in Methods and Results that the preregistered sensitivity analysis was not executed and limit confirmatory claims to the analyses actually completed.

Replace DOI/identifier-only reference entries with a conventional IEEE numbered reference list (authors, title, venue, year) derived from the archived cited records; update in-text citations to IEEE numeric markers. For each in-text citation, confirm and, if necessary, correct that the cited record supports the specific proximate claim (fix any mismatches). Provide the reference list within the five-page manuscript.

Explicitly clarify in Methods (with a pointer to the archived model_configuration.json artifact path and hash already present in the evidence bundle) the runtime sampling semantics: state that temperature was unset (temperature = null) in the recorded configuration, that no explicit deterministic sampling seed was recorded, and therefore nondeterministic model sampling cannot be excluded. This must remain a clear, standalone disclosure in Methods (not only in Limitations).
optional_revisions: Report achieved post-hoc power or a sensitivity/power curve given the observed discordant-pair counts (using archived artifacts) to help readers assess sample-size adequacy.

Include the preregistered secondary analyses (median repair iterations, latency) if archived artifacts permit; if reported, apply the preregistered multiplicity adjustment and clearly label inferential vs exploratory findings.
Provide a short table mapping each numbered reference to the specific claim(s) it was used to support (can be compact), to ease reviewers' verification of citation semantics.
